data.description:
Replace six verbs with one noun and a coherent verb set.

    rebar bridge setup | doctor/fsck | status | preview | sync | pause | resume

Three verbs retire. `reconcile` goes with NO alias, because the defaults invert: `rebar reconcile`
with no arguments means dry-run (the CLI wrapper injects `--mode dry-run` at
`_cli/__init__.py:145-160`, while `python -m rebar_reconciler` itself defaults to LIVE, and
`_lib_ops.py:92` defaults to dry-run again — three entry points, two conventions). `bridge sync`
with no arguments mutates. Aliasing would be a silent behaviour change; anyone with `reconcile` in
a script must re-read the line.

`bridge-status` retires because its producer has never existed in this repo — rebar was extracted
from digital-service-orchestra on 2026-06-08 and the reader was a knowing tombstone from day one.
Note the citation in its docstring, "epic 3a03", is DANGLING: in this repo 3a03 resolves to an
unrelated test-isolation bug created 11 days AFTER the comment citing it. The real epic is
`3006-e198-13db-4e1f`.

`purge-bridge` retires: five commits, every one an automated lint sweep or safety retrofit, none a
feature or bug fix, and no script, workflow, or runbook invokes it. Its `--keep` flag is also
inverted-sense (it deletes everything NOT matching).

`--mode` disappears entirely. Its five values collapse to `preview`/`sync` plus `--max-changes N`;
the two `bootstrap-*` values carry no semantics beyond their cap integer (the only non-applier
consumers test `MODE_CAPS[m] != 0` and never read 10 or 100).

Flags survive only if their help text can be written without internals. Ten candidates reduced to
three: `--max-changes N`, `--only <ids>`, `--except <ids>`, `--max-age <duration>`, plus the house
`--output json`. Maintainer decision: `--only`/`--except` limit what is EXAMINED as well as what is
changed (unlike the internal `--filter-local-ids` they replace, which filtered only writes and was
marked "for validation use only" for that reason), and preview/sync remains the read/write knob.

`check-access` is its own verb, not a flag on the health verb: all three narrowing-flag precedents
(`flux check --pre`, `dbt debug --connection`, `gh auth status`) are READ-ONLY, and none mutates the
remote — so the precedent does not transfer to an operation that creates and deletes a real Jira
issue. `fsck` audits your records; `check-access` proves your access.

`setup` calls `check-access` as its final validation step.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar bridge <verb>` exists with the agreed verb set
- [ ] `reconcile`, `bridge-status`, `purge-bridge` are removed, with release notes; no aliases
- [ ] `--mode` is gone from every surface
- [ ] Every shipped flag's help text contains no internals (no "mode", "rank", "gate", "lock", "cap", "pass", "binding store", no exit-code numbers)
- [ ] `bridge` appears in `rebar --help`; today `reconcile` appears ZERO times while three bridge verbs (one dead) are listed
- [ ] The dangling "epic 3a03" citation is corrected wherever it survives
data.title: Establish the bridge command surface and retire three verbs
